title: Beyond the 956: Brian Tracy, bestselling author of ‘Eat That Frog!,’ dies at 82
excerpt: Brian Tracy, the Canadian-American motivational speaker and bestselling author of ‘Eat That Frog!,’ died November 12, 2026, at 82, according to a statement from Focal Point Business Coaching, the company he co-founded.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Brian Tracy, the Canadian-American motivational speaker and self-development author whose books and seminars reached millions of people around the world, has died at 82.

Tracy died on November 12, 2026, according to a statement from Focal Point Business Coaching, the company he co-founded. He was 82. No cause of death has been publicly stated.

Born January 5, 1944, in Charlottetown, Prince Edward Island, Canada, Tracy left school early and worked a series of labor jobs before studying at the University of Alberta. In 1984 he founded Brian Tracy International in Vancouver, British Columbia, and went on to address more than five million people through thousands of talks and seminars, consulting for more than 1,000 companies.

He authored more than 80 books, translated into dozens of languages. His best-known work, Eat That Frog!: 21 Great Ways to Stop Procrastinating and Get More Done in Less Time, first published in 2001, became an international bestseller and taught millions to tackle their hardest task first. His other titles include Goals!, No Excuses! The Power of Self-Discipline, Maximum Achievement and The Psychology of Achievement.

Tracy is survived by his wife, Barbara, and their four children.

Sources: Focal Point Business Coaching statement; Business Street Magazine; Exchange4Media.
